issues.finding: This is a handled Node relay error, not an unattributed browser crash. Its stack reaches ws emitErrorAndClose, the vendor error listener in lib/tts/wsRelay.ts, and captureTtsRelayFailure. The saved event does not record why CONNECTING was closed.
issues.historicalSource: At retained release 6d5747456c892010939427c2df69f169a48ee1d3, teardown terminates CONNECTING and the vendor error listener reports unconditionally. Commit 33bb388e7625e68bf1c05444b6ca38888e3fd636, already in base 500649965, adds the stopped guard.
issues.localReproduction: The real ws 8.21.0 relay consumer is exercised over loopback with client cancellation and account revocation during a held upstream handshake. Removing only the existing stopped guard produces the exact error text at WebSocket.terminate; the unchanged base passes. Genuine socket hang-up and HTTP 503 failures still report once, a fresh retry sends a segment, and receipt settlement failures still report after teardown.
missingEvidence: The exact client/revocation/provider lifecycle that produced the retained event
issues.nextEvidenceNeeded: Retain lifecycle context if a new occurrence appears after deployment. Local tests establish the guarded cancellation path, not the exact cause or resolution of all 22 historical occurrences.
